newsitem.title: UK: Chemring tumbles after cautious statement.
newsitem.headline: Chemring tumbles after cautious statement.

text.p: Shares in Chemring Group Plc tumbled on Wednesday after the company posted a slim rise in annual profits and warned over a disappointing level of sales in its Chaff Countermeasures defence unit.
The stock was down 45p at 290 by 1003 GMT after falling as low as 285p -- its lowest since December 1994. Trading volume reached 500,000 shares.

Chairman Philip Billington said the group had increased both sales and operating profit in a year when it had suffered a sales setback in its Chaff division due to a delay in orders caused by customer budget constraints.

"The level of sales we are experiencing in Chaff Countermeasures continues to concern us and this fact, together with steps involved in the relocation of this business, will have an influence on our results for the six months to March 1997," Billington said.
"We are hopeful that these delays in defence procurement will resolve themselves during the second half of the year."
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose 3.4 percent in the year ended September 30 to 8.9 million stg on turnover up 13.0 percent at 80.4 million.
The total dividend was raised to 11.45p from 10.90p.
